To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

pharmacological additions (above NRC requirements) of 3, 000 ppm Zn (Zn oxide) or 250 Cu ppm Cu (sulphate) stimulate growth performance beyond that derived from dietary intakes of zinc and copper that meet nutrient requirements for weanling pigs.
pharmacological levels of Zn (3,000 ppm) or Cu (250 ppm) stimulated growth of weanling pig performance beyond that derived from meeting NRC requirements.
feeding pharmacologic levels of Zn and Cu to pigs improves performance and that the response to Zn and the response to Cu are independent of each other.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the use of pharmacological levels of Zn and Cu as growth promoters in weanling pigs.
the effect of pharmacological doses of Zn and Cu on the growth of pigs.
the effect of high levels of zinc and copper on growth performance of young pigs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
pharmacological levels of dietary Cu and Zn stimulate growth performance of weaning pigs.
the pharmacological addition of Zn (3,000 ppm) and(or) Cu (250 ppm) to weanling pig diets improves growth performance and reduces the incidence of diarrhea.
the addition of Zn to diets for weanling pigs stimulates growth performance and reduces the incidence of diarrhea.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
pharmacological additions to the diet of Zn and Cu are beneficial to growth and health of weanling nursery pigs.
Zn and Cu additions to diets for weanling pigs stimulate growth, improve health status, and reduce morbidity and mortality.
pharmacological doses of Cu and Zn can improve growth performance of pigs and may be used to reduce the incidence of diarrhea in weanling pigs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the addition of Zn (3,000 ppm) or Cu (250 ppm) to the weaned pig diet stimulates growth performance.
the addition of Zn or Cu to weanling diets improves pig performance, but the combination of the two minerals does not result in an additional response.
feeding high levels of Zn and Cu is a safe, effective strategy for improving growth of weaned pigs.
